setlist.title: It Must Have Been The Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Feel Like A Stranger** (4 reviews): Described as loping yet funky, with some nice Jerry lead playing; Reviewer says Stranger got into the quad sound early [14][18][19][20]
- **Franklin's Tower** (2 reviews): Reviewer notes Healy finally got Garcia's sound tweaked for Franklin's, or perhaps it was playful volume control; Reviewer finds Franklin's decent but not very dynamic [18][19]
- **La Bamba** (2 reviews): Some friends knock the La Bamba segment, but the reviewer found it hysterical at the time; Seen as a nod to the 1987 Ritchie Valens movie of the same name [16][17]
- **Walkin' Blues** (1 review): Described as not light on its feet, with Brent's playing surging [19]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Followed by a notable extended jam with hints of Playin', considered unusual for 1987 [14]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): The jam at the end of Black Peter is singled out as outstanding [15]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Highlights the Around and Around into Good Lovin' into La Bamba and back into Good Lovin' sequence [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **PITB Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **La Bamba**: back after 1175 archived shows (6144 days); rare: 5 archived performances [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-09-07.nak300.andrewf.73861.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 156 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: Best overall sound among versions; slightly boomy, with Bob's guitar on one side and Brent's keyboard on the other [21]
- **gd87-09-07.aud-sonyecm220t.unknown.8596.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 153 min; rated 3.5/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is sharp and crisp, slightly treble-heavy with some echo, but the crowd is audible; Not the best audience recording the reviewer has heard, but still a nice addition [13][16]
- **gd1987-09-07.176261.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 152 min [3]
- **gd1987-09-07.151412.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 153 min [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer recalls strict open-container enforcement outside, and wonders how they avoided trouble [15]
- Reviewer recalls paying $60 for a ticket that came with blotter, and the acid taking hold during pre-show warm-up [23]
- Reviewer calls it not a landmark show, but a solid opener to a great tour [14]
- Reviewer ranks 9/9/87 as the highlight of the run, with this show as plain fun [16]
- Reviewer says 9/9/87 was incredible, but this show was also a gem [17]
- Notes that 9/9/87 brought first-in-the-run Hey Pocky Way, Blue Dress and Good Golly [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-09-07.nak300.andrewf.73861.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Andrew F; transferred by Andrew F; source: AUD, Nakamichi CM-300's with CP-4 shotgun capsules > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90 cassettes, with no Dolby [1]. Also: Tape flip in Space was patched with the LMA audience source using Soundforge, with fades [1]
- **gd87-09-07.aud-sonyecm220t.unknown.8596.sbeok.shnf**: source: Sony ECM220T mics from taper's section [2]
- **gd1987-09-07.176261.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Doug Lamarre; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Doug Lamarre's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M [3]
- **gd1987-09-07.151412.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Ron Delany Grateful Dead: [1987-09-07 Providence Civic Center, Providence, RI, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-09-07-providence-civic-center-providence-ri-usa/) [25]
- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1987-09-08 Providence Civic Center, Providence, RI, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-09-08-providence-civic-center-providence-ri-usa/) [26]
